settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: Lines 310-321 explicitly reject redirect targets where java.net.URI.getAuthority() is non-null, logging a security warning, which blocks typical absolute URLs like http://evil/.
Lines 318-321 reject values that fail java.net.URI parsing (URISyntaxException), which mitigates many malformed/CRLF-injection inputs.
Line 256 defines REDIRECT_WITH_SCHEME_PATTERN ^(https?://[^/]+)(.*)$ and lines 239-249 split scheme-bearing values, only encoding the path portion via response.encodeRedirectURL.
Could not locate a test proving a bypass, so effective protection cannot be ruled out.
candidates.description: In SlingPostServlet, the redirect target is taken directly from the request parameter SlingPostConstants.RP_REDIRECT_TO (getRedirectUrl, line 309). The code attempts to reject host-bearing targets by constructing a java.net.URI and checking getAuthority() (lines 312-317), and rejects unparsable URIs via URISyntaxException (lines 318-321). If the value passes, it is then reworked (star substitution, request-path prepending, create-suffix handling, lines 325-357) and finally passed to response.sendRedirect(encodedURL) in redirectIfNeeded (line 251). The validation is not a strict relative-path/scheme allow-list: it relies on URI authority presence, and the subsequent transformations can prepend request.getPathInfo() (line 347). This creates a candidate open-redirect / response-splitting concern because the final redirect destination is influenced by a client-supplied parameter and the sink (sendRedirect) is reached whenever the POST operation succeeds. Root cause: partial validation of the redirect parameter rather than enforcing a server-side allow-list of permitted redirect destinations.
missing_evidence: No runtime/test evidence demonstrating a concrete redirect value that passes the authority and URI-syntax checks yet redirects off-site.
Behavior of response.encodeRedirectURL and the container's sendRedirect with respect to authority-free values is not exercised/confirmed.
No analysis of whether request.getPathInfo() prepending (line 347) can be attacker-influenced to form an open redirect when the target does not start with '/'.
preconditions: The Sling POST servlet is reachable for the target resource and the POST operation completes successfully (htmlResponse.isSuccessful()).
Attacker can supply a :redirect (RP_REDIRECT_TO) request parameter.
No upstream filter (e.g., authentication/authorization or a redirect-sanitizing filter) blocks the crafted value before it reaches getRedirectUrl/sendRedirect.
candidates.title: SlingPostServlet HTTP redirect target derived from request parameter with only partial URI validation
